body: The chain walk, on a chain made entirely of bytes the IETF published.

author: reek
body: Every negative below is that same chain with exactly ONE thing changed, which is the only way to know that the rule you think you are testing is the rule that fired.

author: reek
body: An anchor is a name and a key. It is not a certificate: it is trusted because the operator put it there.

author: reek
body: The published chain, at a time inside its validity window. This is the only line here that should say Ok.

author: reek
body: Before the certificate was issued, and after it expired. Told apart, because a certificate that is not valid yet is usually a wrong clock and one that has expired is usually an expired certificate.

author: reek
body: One bit flipped inside the signed body. The signature no longer covers what is there.

author: reek
body: The right key, under a name that does not match the issuer. A chain that reaches no anchor is refused; there is no lenient ending.

author: reek
body: The certificate is not a CA, so it may not issue anything -- checked directly, because we have no second certificate to try to issue.
